correctness.rationale: For any nonempty deleted matching, an acyclic orientation from a missing vertex pair has at most n-1 reachable vertices per source; reverse-order preferred-available-color assignment gives a stable (n-1)-coloring for every profile. For at least two missing pairs, all proper (n-2)-colorings contain at least two doubled classes, each one deleted pair; pairwise reverse rankings force a blocking two-cycle. The complete graph and one-pair boundary cases are handled separately. Correct ordinary chi is n-r. Complete finite corroboration examined 11,888 candidate colorings across nine parameter profiles and verified 3,000 constructive upper-profile instances; code and recorded output are included. The universal proof is analytic.

originality.rationale: The first public source is Koana, Oh and Yoneda, arXiv:2609.00569v1, posted 2026-09-01. Its Section 3.1 gives a universal reachability upper bound, and Section 3.4 gives exact values for paths, cycles and complete bipartite graphs, including the K_4 minus a perfect matching base case. The matching-deletion family for arbitrary n,r, and its adversarial reverse-pair lower bound, is not stated in the inspected exact-family results. Targeted external and semantic finding searches did not identify a stronger or equivalent family theorem; this is a conditional literature assessment, not a priority certificate.

value.rationale: A complete, parameter-uniform exact classification for the canonical graph family K_n minus a matching, including all cocktail-party graphs, determines an emerging preference-sensitive graph invariant on a natural dense family. Unlike ordinary chi=n-r, stable chi remains n-1 whenever at least one edge is deleted, producing an unbounded additive gap r-1 and an explicit structural two-cycle obstruction to reusing two missing pairs. The result is not just a relabeling of the general reachability bound, whose lower side it supplies separately.
